newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks close firm, off intraday highs.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks close firm, off intraday highs.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed ahead, but off their intraday highs in active trading that saw brewer Bavaria SA among the movers in Bogota.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose 0.53 percent to 15,969.57 in volume of over 2.0 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB rose 0.55 percent, meanwhile, ending the day at 1,027.19. Volume in Bogota was 2.2 billion pesos.
"The market behaved in a very fickle way," said one Bogota-based trader. "We had record highs for some shares and then they fell." He added: "I didn't see things clearly at all."
Bavaria, which led gainers in Bogota, closed up 3.07 percent at 6,700 pesos per share in a price move that saw 677 million pesos of shares change hands.
"The stock has buyers and sellers and clients of all kinds," said the trader, who described Bavaria as the country's most liquid share.

Compania Suramericana de Seguros, the insurance giant belonging to the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, was also actively traded in Bogota, but it closed unchanged at 21,000 pesos per share.

Big winners in Bogota, along with Bavaria, included Bancoquia, which ended up 2.54 percent at 2,820 pesos a share. The bank performed even better in Medellin, however, ending up 2.95 percent at 2,831.
Cementos Caribe closed up 1.67 percent in Medellin and Compania Nacional de Chocolates rose 1.12 percent to close at 9,000 per share.
Bancoquia, Caribe and Chocolates all belong to the Sindicato Antioqueno group, which brokers say is heavily favored by foreign funds.
